A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Tree Search for Language Model Agents. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original agent evaluations on VisualWebArena and WebArena, quantitative ablations, and additional model combinations and qualitative results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark evaluations and ablations, including the search results in Table 2 and additional agent/value-function combinations in Appendix Table 8.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same best-first search, action generation, value function, and termination procedure. Appendix A.4.1 expands the reset-and-replay implementation already described in v2 Section 5.4; it does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the full 910 VisualWebArena and 812 WebArena tasks across the same websites, with 200-task VisualWebArena ablations. Newly cited AndroidWorld and SciBench are not added to the experiments.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds published WebArena comparisons with GUI-API Hybrid Agent, AgentOccam, and AgentOccam-Judge. Existing comparators remain. Trajectory reranking was already evaluated in v2 Appendix A.2.2 and is only moved into the main text.

E3.justification: The reported search budgets, action limits, sampling settings, model configurations, and ablation protocols remain unchanged. The reranking experiment retains its settings; v3's added statement about approximate compute parity does not establish a revised evaluation design.

E4.justification: The search-budget, depth/breadth, value-function, difficulty, website, and qualitative analyses are retained. The reranking analysis moves from v2 Appendix A.2.2/Figure 6 to v3 Section 5.1/Figure 3 with the same experimental evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The retained self-consistency sample counts and sampled trajectories concern the inference procedure, not newly introduced statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes SteP from 35.8% to 33.5% and adds GUI-API Hybrid Agent at 35.8%, AgentOccam at 43.1%, and AgentOccam-Judge at 45.7%. Section 4.2 corrects the VisualWebArena baseline from 18.6% to 18.9%, matching Table 2. The proposed agents' scores remain unchanged. v3 Appendix Table 8 still reports SteP at 35.8%, creating an inconsistency.

T1.justification: The environment definitions, deterministic-transition assumption, value-function equations, and formal search algorithm remain substantively unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs that are added or revised in the other.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of effective inference-time search in realistic web environments, compatibility with existing agents, and scaling with test-time compute. The headline VisualWebArena and WebArena performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 newly explains that the screenshot-based web value function may transfer poorly to software-engineering tasks and may need domain-specific evidence such as execution traces. Section 4.2 also more explicitly positions stronger agents' engineered inputs as potentially complementary to search.

D1.justification: Appendix A.4.1 adds details about storing scored action sequences and replaying them during resets. Section 5.1 newly states approximate compute parity for search c=5 and reranking n=5. Conversely, v3 omits the ablation subset's 100/50/50 website breakdown and shortens observation examples in Figures 8–9. Code access remains stated.

R1.justification: v3 adds AndroidWorld, LiteSearch, SciBench, ReST-MCTS*, and the works underlying the new WebArena comparator rows, while removing The Dawn of LMMs reference. These extend the surrounding literature and comparison context without substantially redefining the work's positioning.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized prose cuts and refinements, moves reranking into Section 5.1, adds the reset subsection, and replaces the Ethics Statement heading with Statement of Broader Impact. The acknowledgments and standalone reproducibility statement disappear, but the overall narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The document is extensively reformatted into the TMLR style, changing typography, text width, author layout, running headers, and figure/table sizing and placement. Figure 1 is rearranged with the instruction and legend beside the trajectories, and the reranking plot moves into the main text. Reflow also leaves v3 page 9 largely empty.

improvement.justification: Broader baseline context, the explicit domain-transfer limitation, and clearer reset implementation provide a limited overall gain in scientific clarity. These benefits are tempered by omitted ablation and prompt details and the inconsistent SteP scores across Tables 2 and 8. The original experimental evidence is largely unchanged; moving reranking into the main text does not add validation.
